title: Station network health — INAMHI (Ecuador)
description: Ecuador's hydrometeorological network read live: what the service says is transmitting, and what each hydrological station actually answers when asked.

list.name: estacion
list.label: Station
list.description: Only the stations the service reports as transmitting — there is no point offering a drill-down into one that publishes nothing. The default is a hydrological station with a river reach, which is the only kind that fills all four panels below: level, battery, sensor list and forecast.
list.query:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
-- Es la misma lista que alimenta el visor de INAMHI, así que el tablero nunca
-- puede hablar de una estación que el organismo no publique.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
SELECT (e->>'punto_obs') || '  ·  ' || (e->>'codigo') AS __text,
       (e->>'id_estacion')                            AS __value
FROM inv
WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO'
ORDER BY __text

list.name: parametro
list.label: Sensor
list.description: The chosen station's live sensors. Rebuilt whenever the station changes, so the list can never offer a sensor this particular box does not carry.
list.query:
LOAD http_client;
-- Los sensores que la estación elegida tiene VIVOS. El filtro de treinta días
-- no es cosmético: hay cajas que siguen publicando sondas de suelo paradas en
-- 2016, y sin él encabezan la lista.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/parametros/?id_estacion='
                  || '${estacion}' || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS resp
), s AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    coalesce(nullif(resp->>'body', ''), '[]'), '$[*].params[*]')) AS p
  FROM r
)
SELECT (p->>'descripcion_parametro') AS __text,
       (p->>'nemonico')              AS __value
FROM s
WHERE strptime((p->>'fecha_ultimo_dato')[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
      > timezone('UTC', now()) - INTERVAL 30 DAY
ORDER BY __text
list.definition: sensores con dato en los últimos 30 días

options.content:
# Station network health — INAMHI

Ecuador's hydrometeorological network, read live from the API behind INAMHI's own
[Visor Hidrometeorológico](https://inamhi.gob.ec/info/). **1,894 stations** are on the books;
the service labels **224** of them as transmitting.

That label is what this dashboard is about. It is the network's own account of itself, and it is
not quite true: a station marked *TRANSMITIENDO* can be nine hours behind, and some return no
sensor list at all. The map and the counters below show the label. The table further down stops
trusting it and **asks each hydrological station directly** how old its newest reading is.

Nothing here is stored or pre-computed — every panel is a live call, and the public history stops
at ten days.

panels.title: The network on paper
panels.description: Straight from the inventory call: what exists, and what the service says is alive.

targets.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
-- Es la misma lista que alimenta el visor de INAMHI, así que el tablero nunca
-- puede hablar de una estación que el organismo no publique.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
SELECT
  count(*)                                                                   AS "Stations",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO')       AS "Transmitting",
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO')
        / count(*), 1)                                                       AS "Share (%)",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO'
                     AND (e->>'categoria') LIKE '%HIDRO%')                   AS "Hydrological"
FROM inv

panels.title: The network as INAMHI labels it
panels.description: Every station on the books, coloured by the transmission status the service publishes. One request, 1,894 points. Switch to 'by kind' in the layer list to see how the hydrological stations sit on the rivers.

panels.title: Where the live stations are
panels.description: Transmitting stations by province. Twelve provinces of the twenty-four hold almost all of it.

targets.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
-- Es la misma lista que alimenta el visor de INAMHI, así que el tablero nunca
-- puede hablar de una estación que el organismo no publique.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
-- Dónde está viva la red. El reparto no es geográfico sino presupuestario:
-- Pichincha concentra casi un tercio de todo lo que transmite.
SELECT e->>'provincia' AS key, count(*) AS n
FROM inv
WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 12

panels.title: Who keeps them running
panels.description: Total stations and how many still transmit, by owner. INAMHI is not the only one: CELEC and the old EX-INERHI hold a large share of the books.

targets.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
-- Es la misma lista que alimenta el visor de INAMHI, así que el tablero nunca
-- puede hablar de una estación que el organismo no publique.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
)
-- La red no es toda de INAMHI: hay estaciones de EX-INERHI, de CELEC y de otros
-- organismos. Esta es la lectura que no se ve en el visor — quién mantiene qué,
-- y qué parte de lo suyo sigue en pie.
SELECT e->>'propietario' AS key,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO')     AS "Transmitting",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') <> 'TRANSMITIENDO')    AS "Silent"
FROM inv
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY "Transmitting" + "Silent" DESC
LIMIT 10

panels.title: Measured, not labelled — the hydrological stations
panels.description: The 43 hydrological stations that claim to be transmitting, each asked directly how old its newest reading is. This panel takes 8–11 s: it makes 43 calls, one per station, because the API has no bulk endpoint for freshness. Anything red is a station that says it is alive and is not keeping up.

targets.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- El inventario entero en UNA petición: 1.894 estaciones, 768 KB, medio segundo.
-- Es la misma lista que alimenta el visor de INAMHI, así que el tablero nunca
-- puede hablar de una estación que el organismo no publique.
--
-- OJO con los paréntesis: `->>` tiene MENOS precedencia que `LIKE`, así que
-- `e->>'categoria' LIKE '%HIDRO%'` se parsea como `e ->> ('categoria' LIKE ...)`
-- e intenta usar un booleano como índice: "Failed to cast value to numerical".
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/visores/?id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh')->>'body', '$[*]')) AS e
),
-- Las hidrológicas que DICEN transmitir. Son 43 y a cada una se le pregunta por
-- separado: no existe endpoint que dé la frescura de toda la red de golpe
-- (`parametros/` sin `id_estacion` responde 400).
hidro AS (
  SELECT (e->>'id_estacion')::BIGINT AS id_estacion,
         e->>'codigo'    AS codigo,
         e->>'punto_obs' AS nombre,
         e->>'provincia' AS provincia
  FROM inv
  WHERE (e->>'estado_transmision') = 'TRANSMITIENDO'
    AND (e->>'categoria') LIKE '%HIDRO%'
),
-- Un GET por estación, en serie dentro de la misma consulta: 43 peticiones,
-- entre 8 y 11 s medidos. Por eso este panel es el único que tarda, y por eso
-- no se extiende a las 224 que transmiten en total: serían ~29 s y tocarían el
-- plazo de Grafana.
probed AS (
  SELECT h.*,
         http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/parametros/?id_estacion='
                  || h.id_estacion || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS r
  FROM hidro h
),
-- El `coalesce` de dos pisos es el que salva a los muertos: una estación que
-- devuelve cuerpo vacío se queda con lista vacía en vez de desaparecer. Con un
-- LATERAL/unnest en su lugar, esas filas se esfuman sin avisar — justo las que
-- este panel existe para enseñar.
medido AS (
  SELECT codigo, nombre, provincia, (r->>'status') AS status,
         coalesce(
           json_extract_string(coalesce(nullif(r->>'body', ''), '[]'),
                               '$[*].params[*].fecha_ultimo_dato'),
           []::VARCHAR[]) AS sellos
  FROM probed
),
-- `fecha_ultimo_dato` llega etiquetada `-05:00`, pero ese reloj ES UTC: si se
-- creyera el sufijo, el último dato caería cinco horas en el futuro. Se corta a
-- 19 caracteres y se compara contra UTC.
fechas AS (
  SELECT *, list_max(list_transform(sellos,
             s -> strptime(s[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'))) AS ultimo
  FROM medido
)
SELECT codigo      AS "Code",
       nombre      AS "Station",
       provincia   AS "Province",
       len(sellos) AS "Sensors",
       ultimo      AS "Last datum (UTC)",
       round(date_diff('minute', ultimo, timezone('UTC', now())) / 60.0, 1) AS "Hours behind"
FROM fechas
ORDER BY "Hours behind" DESC NULLS FIRST

panels.title: The chosen station, the chosen sensor
panels.description: Hourly readings straight from the station. The public history stops at ten days — ask for more and the service answers 401, which reaches the panel as an empty chart.

panels.title: Battery
panels.description: Supply voltage, where the station reports it — about two in five do. It is the one reading that is about the station itself rather than the weather, and a sagging battery is what precedes a station going quiet.

panels.title: Sensor by sensor
panels.description: Every sensor in the chosen station and how far behind each one is. Transmitting is a property of the box, not of its sensors: a station can be an hour fresh on rainfall and years stale on soil temperature.

targets.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- Los sensores de la estación elegida, con lo viejo que es el dato de cada uno.
-- Aquí se ve que "transmitiendo" es una propiedad de la ESTACIÓN y no de sus
-- sensores: en una misma caja conviven el pluviómetro de hace una hora y la
-- sonda de suelo parada desde 2016.
--
-- $estacion va a pelo: en una consulta de panel el datasource la entrecomilla
-- solo, así que queda '62541' y concatena sin más.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/station_information/estaciones/parametros/?id_estacion='
                  || $estacion || '&id_aplicacion=vs_1h_inh') AS resp
), s AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(
    coalesce(nullif(resp->>'body', ''), '[]'), '$[*].params[*]')) AS p
  FROM r
)
SELECT p->>'descripcion_parametro' AS "Sensor",
       p->>'simbolo_unidad'        AS "Unit",
       strptime((p->>'fecha_ultimo_dato')[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S') AS "Last datum (UTC)",
       round(date_diff('minute',
             strptime((p->>'fecha_ultimo_dato')[1:19], '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'),
             timezone('UTC', now())) / 60.0, 1) AS "Hours behind"
FROM s
ORDER BY "Hours behind"

panels.title: Forecast discharge — GEOGLOWS
panels.description: Fifteen days of modelled discharge for the river reach attached to this station, three-hourly, with its uncertainty band. The dashboard window reaches into the future so this has somewhere to be drawn; measurement stops at now, the forecast carries on. Only the hydrological stations that have a reach return anything; for the rest this panel is empty on purpose.

targets.rawSql:
LOAD http_client;
-- GEOGLOWS solo contesta por las estaciones que tienen un tramo de río asociado
-- —27 de las 651 hidrológicas—; al resto les responde 404 con su motivo:
-- "La estación no tiene un river_id asociado". Ese 404 es la respuesta CORRECTA,
-- no una avería, así que este panel se sirve por DuckDB y no por Infinity: el
-- guardián de estado lo convierte en cero filas en vez de en un aspa roja que
-- contradiría lo que promete la descripción del panel.
WITH r AS (
  SELECT http_get('https://inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor/geoglows/forecast/station/' || $estacion || '/') AS resp
), ok AS (
  SELECT resp->>'body' AS body FROM r WHERE (resp->>'status') = '200'
), pts AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(body, '$.data[*]')) AS d FROM ok
)
SELECT (d->>'date')::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time,
       (d->>'median')::DOUBLE    AS median,
       (d->>'lower')::DOUBLE     AS lower,
       (d->>'upper')::DOUBLE     AS upper
FROM pts
ORDER BY time

options.content:
**Source** — INAMHI, *Visor Hidrometeorológico* (`inamhi.gob.ec/api_visor`), read live.
Forecast discharge from **GEOGLOWS**, served by INAMHI for the 27 hydrological stations that have
a river reach attached to them.

**What the numbers do not say.** *Transmitting* is the organisation's own label and is not a
measurement: the table is. Public history is capped at **ten days** — a longer range returns 401,
not an error the panel can explain. Timestamps in the sensor listing arrive tagged `-05:00` on a
clock that is really UTC, so both tables correct it rather than repeat it. And a handful of
stations report impossible rainfall — a sensor fault the service passes through unfiltered — so
a single station's spike is not evidence of weather.

**One station in twenty answers nothing.** Pick one of those and the sensor list comes back empty,
the *Sensor* dropdown has nothing to offer, and the sensor chart flags an error rather than drawing
a blank — the query has no sensor code to ask for. That is the dashboard telling the truth about a
station the network still counts as transmitting.
